programme.desc: Pugsley and Wednesday start a row at a party when their gift of a tarantula upsets Harold, the birthday boy. Harold's parents insist that the Addams children lack breeding and, therefore, are no longer allowed to play with their son.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: Para evitar que Emiliano se declare inocente y la policía descubra quienes son los verdaderos culpables del lavado de dólares, los socios de Corona deciden contratar a los mariachis y en medio de la serenata, se toman fotos junto a Rosario.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: Emiliano es visitado por Corona y éste le muestra las fotos en que Rosario aparece junto a los cabecillas de la organización. Emiliano no tendrá otra opción que acceder a las pretensiones del abogado. Por otro lado, Rosario recibe la visa mexicana.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: El comandante Salas revisa el interrogatorio y empieza a dudar de la culpabilidad de Emiliano. Por otro lado, Rosario no puede entrar al reclusorio por ser Emiliano un preso de alta seguridad. Rosario buscara la ayuda de la teniente Morales.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: El encuentro en la cárcel entre Emiliano y Rosario resulta muy corto, y sirve para confirmar que la pareja se ama igual que antes. No obstante, el mariachi le advierte a su novia que lo mejor para ella es que no se vuelvan a ver.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: Rosario regresa a Colombia y es bien recibida por todos sus compañeros. Por otro lado, el doctor Javier Macías le dice a Don Carlos que deben liquidar el bar cuanto antes para poder asumir las deudas que tiene.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: Los muchachos de la manada intentan encontrar la forma para salvar el bar Garibaldi y dentro de esta búsqueda Rosario descubre que el culpable de esta crisis financiera es el Doctor Macías. Por otro lado, llega el día del juicio de Emiliano.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: Al enterarse de la condena que tendrá que asumir Emiliano por unos crímenes que no cometió, Sigifredo y Fernando le escriben un correo electrónico anónimo al comandante Salas, comentándole que está cometiendo una gran injusticia.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: Con dolor en sus corazones, los mariachis del bar Garibaldi se despiden. Rosario vende el traje de su papá para pagar la deuda que tiene con Javier Macías. Por otra parte, el comandante Salas decide reabrir la investigación del caso de Emiliano.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: Han transcurrido varios meses desde el cierre del bar Garibaldi. Los integrantes de la manada no la pasan bien en sus nuevas vidas. Por otro lado, el Comandante Salas visita a Emiliano para decirle que ya sabe toda la verdad de su caso.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: Las autoridades capturan a Miguel Corona y sus socios. Emiliano y Felipe recobran su libertad. Por otra parte, un empresario mexicano reabrirá el bar plaza Garibaldi.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: Alejandro Villa Ruiz, el empresario que compró el bar Plaza Garibaldi, reúne a todos los integrantes del grupo de mariachis para hablarles sobre sus contratos. Además el empresario va en busca de don Carlos Malagón para proponerle que sea su socio.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: Emiliano aparece por sorpresa vestido de Mariachi y con varias canciones le recuerda a Rosario que ella es la mujer de su vida. Emiliano y Rosario ahora podrán disfrutar de ese sentimiento que por las injusticias de la vida tuvieron que retener.

programme.title: La hija del mariachi
programme.desc: Emiliano otorga grandes regalos a todas aquellas personas que en su paso por Colombia lo ayudaron. Por otro lado, llega la noche esperada por todos, la velada en la que el Bar Plaza Garibaldi abrirá nuevamente sus puertas al público.

Viewing the local Native Americans through an ignorantly negative lens, Thursday is determined to engage them in battle for his own glory, despite the warnings of York -- an act of folly that will have dire consequences.

programme.title: Shane
programme.desc: Enigmatic gunslinger Shane (Alan Ladd) rides into a small Wyoming town with hopes of quietly settling down as a farmhand. Taking a job on homesteader Joe Starrett's (Van Heflin) farm, Shane is drawn into a battle between the townsfolk and ruthless cattle baron Rufus Ryker (Emile Meyer). Shane's growing attraction to Starrett's wife, Marian (Jean Arthur), and his fondness for their son Joey (Brandon de Wilde), who idolizes Shane, force Shane to realize that he must thwart Ryker's plan.

programme.title: Gold of the Seven Saints
programme.desc: After discovering a fortune in gold nuggets, Shaun Garrett (Roger Moore) and his partner, Jim Rainbolt (Clint Walker), make their way toward the town of Seven Saints to redeem it for cash. Word of their find reaches bandit McCracken (Gene Evans), who comes after them. The men hide their treasure and fend off McCracken with the help of Doc Gates (Chill Wills), before escaping to recover at the ranch of Rainbolt's friend, Amos Gondora (Robert Middleton), waiting until they can retrieve the gold.

programme.title: Yellowstone Kelly
programme.desc: Union soldier Maj. Towns (Rhodes Reason) asks fur trapper and Indian scout Luther "Yellowstone" Kelly (Clint Walker) to scout for the Army in Sioux territory. Kelly ventures into the area, only to be taken prisoner by the Sioux. Since Kelly saved the life of Chief Gall (John Russell) years before, the chief promises to free him if Kelly treats wounded Arapaho maiden Wahleeah (Andra Martin). Soon Kelly and the recovered Wahleeah are caught between Towns' soldiers and the vengeful Sioux.

programme.title: Back To School
programme.desc: When the NEXO-Knights are sloppy in a fight with Jestro, Merlok 2.0 sends them back to the Knights' Academy. Not only for a brush-up but to find out what Jestro is after in its hallowed halls. As they Knights battle Jestro – in a somewhat haphazard and lazy way – they discuss the fact that Jestro never wins and that they're always getting over on him. Despite defeating the jerky Jester and his evil Book, Merlok 2.0 discovers that something about the attack on the village is tied to the Knights' Academy. It looks like that's where they'll strike next. It wouldn't hurt for the Knights to go “back to school” to watch for Jestro and for some refresher training. Merlok is sure Jestro wants something at the Academy, but he doesn't know what it is. The Knights are very much “fish out of water” at the academy, even with the “cool kids” – Robin and Ava – showing them around. The next generation of Knights is being taught to integrate the NEXO-Magic of Merlok into their fighting techniques and these kids are good (so good, they initially kick the lazy, know-it-all Knight's butts!) Their old principal, the ever-ornery Headmaster Brickland, sets them straight: they're all still slackers, and they better get their acts together (especially Lance!) The Knights take shifts as “library helpers” much to the delight of the old squirebot librarian, MARGE. They're convinced Jestro is after a book…isn't he always after a book? When Jestro attacks, the Knights help organize the students and there's a big fight in the Academy Library versus Jestro and his Monsters. They drive Jestro off without letting him steal any books! Victory! But as Jestro leaves, we see him holding what the Book of Monsters really wanted: a snow globe with a castle in it that was sitting on the librarian's desk. In the Lava Lands, Jestro throws the snow globe into a volcano and it frees the massive Castle of Monstrux from its snowy magic prison

programme.title: How Jesus Became God
programme.sub-title: Jesus - The Man Who Became God
programme.desc: The historical significance of the Christian belief in Jesus's divinity, in terms of its effects on Western civilization; learning about different scholarly views of the historical Jesus; tracing the diversity of early Christian thought.

programme.title: How Jesus Became God
programme.desc: The accounts of divine mortals in the ancient world; the overlap between the human and divine worlds in Greco-Roman polytheistic religions; exploring three age-old models of divine men in both mythology and Christian scripture.

programme.title: How Jesus Became God
programme.sub-title: Humans as Gods in the Greco-Roman World
programme.desc: Delving into the interface between the human and the divine in pagan cultures; examining narratives describing people born of the sexual union of gods with mortals; looking at cases of humans who were exalted to the status of gods.

programme.title: How Jesus Became God
programme.sub-title: Gods Who Were Human in Ancient Judaism
programme.desc: Accounts of divine humans and other godlike beings within ancient Judaism; exploring conceptions of divine beings that appear in human form in Genesis and Exodus; studying narratives of humans who become angelic beings in other Jewish texts.

programme.title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
programme.desc: This lecture introduces some issues essential to understanding how Christianity begins; growing away from its Jewish roots; ultimately becoming the most important religion of the civilization.

programme.title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
programme.sub-title: The Religious World of Early Christianity
programme.desc: This lecture introduces the pagan, polytheistic religions that dominate the early world; the most important Roman religion for the birth of Christianity; Judaism, the religion of Jesus and his followers.

programme.title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
programme.desc: In the first of three lectures on the birth of Christianity, Professor Ehrman examines the life of Jesus of Nazareth; referred to both outside the New Testament and within the Gospels themselves.

programme.title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
programme.sub-title: Oral and Written Traditions about Jesus
programme.desc: How four anonymous authors who live decades after Jesus record traditions that have been circulating orally over the intervening years; examining the extent to which those traditions have been modified in the retelling.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.desc: The course begins by addressing some of the basic facts about the New Testament; which books it contains, when they are written, in what language and by whom.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.desc: The Epistles of Paul are the earliest books of the New Testament, predating even the Gospels; the realities of writing a letter in the ancient world; issues that affect how one understands Paul's Epistles and the other writings of the New Testament.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.desc: This lecture looks at some of the major teachings of Paul's Epistles; showing how he shapes his theological and ethical views in light of the problems that emerge in his burgeoning Christian communities.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.desc: This lecture considers the broad problem of pseudonymity, or forgery, in the ancient world; applying one's findings to the Pauline letters of the New Testament to see if any, in fact, are written by Paul's followers rather than Paul himself.

programme.title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
programme.desc: The historical trajectory of Christianity; contemporary ignorance of its past; considering the value of the historical study of Christianity; looking at the methods and role of the historian; the sources and limitations of historical knowledge.

programme.title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
programme.sub-title: The First Cultural Context - Greece and Rome
programme.desc: Investigating the culture of the Mediterranean world in which Christianity is born; the legacy of Alexander; the features of Greek politics, religion and philosophy; learning about the nature of Roman rule and imperial order in the region.

programme.title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
programme.desc: The circumstances of Jewish life in ancient Palestine and the diaspora; examining cultural and ideological factors that divide the Jews; the tensions they face between assimilation and separation; their resistance to Greek culture and Roman rule.

programme.title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
programme.sub-title: The Jesus Movement and the Birth of Christianity
programme.desc: Considering the resurrection as marking the birth of Christianity, as rooted in the claims of the first believers; assessing the contradiction between Jesus as the source of divine life and the degrading manner of his death.
